feature: Typed text is readable in every dashboard field
summary: Every field on the status dashboard now shows what you type in the normal text color instead of black on a black well, in both the dark and the light theme.
setup: The design dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8791. Nothing to enable. Try it once in your normal theme, then flip your Mac between Dark and Light in System Settings > Appearance and try it again.

try.do: Open the Tasks section and type a title into 'What should get done?'.
Type a couple of lines into the notes box under it.
Type into 'Filter tasks' at the top right of the All tasks list.
Click any task row, then type a number into the Seq field at the bottom of the dialog.
Open Ready to try, click the speech bubble on any line, and type into the box that opens.
On Summary, if a decision is waiting, type into the 'Optional note' box on an option.
Switch your Mac between Dark and Light and read all six again.

evaluate: Can you read every character as you type it, in both themes?
The notes box and the feedback box are now a little taller than before, because they take the system's own multiline height. Does that feel right, or was the shorter two-line box better?
The text in these fields is now the same size and typeface as the rest of the dashboard. Does the page read as one thing now?
Is the focus ring around a field clear enough to tell you where your typing is going?
rough: This was a plain bug, not a design change: the shared field style paints the dark recessed well on a wrapper and the ink on the field inside it, and four fields wore the style on the field itself, so they got the well and kept the browser's black text.
The only visible change beyond color is height and typeface on the two multiline boxes, which now match every other multiline field in the system.

A check now fails the build if anyone puts a wrapper style on a bare field again, for all seven components that work this way, and the rule is written into the component file and the design-system guide.
The pictures are real screenshots of the real dashboard taken in Chrome, not renders. This surface is a web page, so no macOS screen recording grant was involved.
The decision card in the third picture is a fake one injected only so the note field could be typed into: no real decision was waiting at the time, and nothing was answered.
